newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares edge up, rally hit by profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares edge up, rally hit by profit-taking.

text.p: Many leading Russian shares closed higher on Tuesday, but traders said profit-taking slowed the rally towards the end of the day and that the market was likely to pause for breath before increasing further.

"Today's (late) fall was caused by the desire of local brokers, who had already positioned themselves, to take profits after the sharp rise in the absence of mass Western demand and active share turnover," said Andrei Kukk, head of equity trading at Rinaco Plus.
The Russian Trading System 22-share index closed at 339.04 after 334.59 on Monday. Total market turnover was $44.4 million, considered a healthy level for Russia's emerging market.
But traders saw a short-term correction beginning after the spurt of the last few days.

"The market has got to correct and prices have got to halt. One way or another the short-term interest has been fulfilled: everyone has made their money and everyone is happy," said Renaissance Capital trader Vladimir Chkikvadze.
National power utility UES EESR.RTS rose to $0.2740 from $0.2720 on Monday, while international long-distance telecom Rostelekom RTKM.RTS edged up to $3.92 from $3.89.
Regional power company Mosenergo MSNG.RTS slipped to $1.351 from $1.352.
Kukk said he saw telecom prices fluctuating in the leadup to the sale of a 49 percent stake in holding company Svyazinvest, and did not rule out the index closing lower on Wednesday.
But traders said the market would not fall back to recent lows, and was set to grow further in the short term.
"This is not the last we've seen of it -- UES is not going to cost 25 cents any more and Mosenergo is not going to be $1.20," said Kukk.
